comparator.name: Global Responsibility and Leadership
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Groningen page confirms that the programme has been renamed Global Politics & Sustainability while retaining CROHO 59327. For the fixed Fall 2026 cohort, the 2026–2027 Ocasys catalogue still identifies the BSc as Global Responsibility and Leadership, and the official GRL curriculum brochure documents its three-major structure. The generic target does not select a major, so the first-listed major, Energy, Ecology & Climate, is instantiated by official order before considering UCR fit. The curriculum comprises 50 EC of named first-year foundations, 65 EC of genuine major-elective space, 15 EC of Personal Leadership Lab, Statistics II and Ethics and Global Responsibility, a 10-EC Living Lab, a 30-EC minor, and a 10-EC capstone thesis portfolio. These components account for 50 + 65 + 15 + 10 + 30 + 10 = 180 EC. Major-elective slots remain explicit rather than inventing course choices.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic GRL degree and does not specify one of its three formal majors. The official curriculum lists Energy, Ecology & Climate first, before Politics, Philosophy & Economics and Culture, Psychology & Global Health; it is therefore selected before and independently of UCR fit.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Global responsibility, leadership and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals
Sustainable development, climate action, energy transition and environmental sustainability
Global governance, political power, accountability, economics and institutions
Ethical responses to global challenges, justice, inclusion and inequality
Human behaviour, culture, psychology, health and wellbeing in social and environmental context
Interdisciplinary qualitative, statistical, digital and real-world research methods
Local solutions, circular economy, Living Lab co-creation and social innovation
Personal leadership development and a capstone portfolio integrating research and responsibility
adjacent: Energy, Ecology & Climate as a formal major
Politics, Philosophy & Economics as a formal major
Culture, Psychology & Global Health as a formal major
Community-based and globally connected applied work
questions: How can climate, energy and ecological transitions be designed responsibly?
How do power, ethics, economics and institutions shape responsible global action?
How can behaviour, culture, health and community collaboration support inclusive change?

selection.assessment: The first-listed Energy, Ecology & Climate major is the closest match. The two remaining formal majors—Politics, Philosophy & Economics and Culture, Psychology & Global Health—each generate a coherent, feasible and materially distinct UCR pathway. All direct interests are owned by the common core, and all three stable study directions are represented. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: Energy, ecology & climate
alternatives.labelReason: Earth and environmental science, water, ecology, energy transition, sustainability and resource governance form the organising core, with economics, data and quantitative methods supporting environmental decisions. This is the closest feasible response to the first-listed official GRL major.
alternatives.concept: A science-and-policy route for understanding climate, Earth systems, biodiversity, water, energy and resource transitions, combining environmental research with economics, data analysis and sustainability governance.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort offerings were checked against the enriched workbook. Earth, sustainability, economics, mathematics and data foundations precede GIS, hydrology, resource analysis, upper-level research and governance; PPD is in Year 1 and at least six courses are level 300.

alternatives.label: Politics, philosophy & economics
alternatives.labelReason: Political theory, comparative politics, international relations, law and economics form the organising core, with history, sociology, research and public communication supporting the official GRL major.
alternatives.concept: A governance-centred route addressing global inequality, institutions, international law, ethical responsibility, conflict and political economy through political science, philosophy, law, economics and social research.
alternatives.distinctness: The route replaces most Earth-system, ecology, water, climate and resource-science courses with politics, law, philosophy, history and political economy. It differs from the closest route by well over the required four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Formal prerequisites and fixed-cohort offerings were checked. Gateways precede international, constitutional and EU law, public economics, econometrics, EU politics and peace and conflict. PPD is in Year 1 and at least six courses are level 300.

alternatives.label: Culture, psychology & global health
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines social psychology, human behaviour, biomedicine and global health with sociology, culture, media, communication, law, history and sustainability. It directly reflects the third formal GRL major without implying an official UCR major.
alternatives.concept: A social and health route examining behaviour, culture, inequality, global health and community change through psychology, biomedicine, sociology, media, law, sustainability and qualitative and quantitative research.
progression: Formal prerequisites and Fall-2026-cohort offerings were checked against the enriched workbook. Research, social-science and life-science foundations precede upper-level psychology, sociology, history, environment and conflict courses; PPD is in Year 1 and at least six courses are level 300.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces the closest route’s concentrated Earth-system, ecology, energy, water and resource-science sequence with psychology, biomedicine, sociology, health, culture, media, law and communication. It also differs substantially from the Politics, Philosophy and Economics route in both subject core and methods.

notes.text: Groningen embeds a formal 65-EC major, two leadership labs, an external-partner Living Lab, a 30-EC minor and a capstone thesis portfolio within one residential Liberal Arts and Sciences degree. UCR can assemble three rigorous 180-EC pathways around the same academic directions, but they are illustrative UCR curricula rather than Groningen majors and do not reproduce the Campus Fryslân Living Lab and portfolio structure.
